questions.prompt: Use Trials 1 and 3 as evidence. Name the one variable that changed and the variables held constant, report both lifting results, and explain what the iron core does to the field and why the measured current stayed the same.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Evidence must compare the recorded Trial 1 and Trial 3 results. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2.
a. Full credit: Identifies core material as the only changed variable, names the controls, reports 49 and 4 clips, explains that iron concentrates the field, and explains that current stayed the same because the electrical resistance and voltage were unchanged. Partial credit: Gives the correct pattern but omits data, controls, or the current explanation. No credit: Compares uncontrolled trials or claims the iron core caused the current change.

questions.prompt: Defend the design with your highest strength-to-cost ratio. Compare at least three different tested designs, giving each design's turns, core, diameter, cells, wiring, clips lifted, cost, and calculated clips / cost to 2 decimals. Show the percentage improvement of your best ratio over the Trial 1 baseline using unrounded ratios from displayed costs, rounding the final percentage to 1 decimal. Explain why maximizing lifting strength alone can give worse value. State whether you reached the 6.38 clips-per-cost target and support your conclusion with your checked results.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Grade the calculation method, comparison of three tested designs, and explanation of strength versus cost. Several designs can share the same score rounded to 2 decimals. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3.
a. Full credit: Compares at least three complete tested designs with accurate clips, costs, and calculated ratios; identifies the best ratio; correctly calculates percentage improvement using (best ratio / (49 / 14.14) - 1) x 100; reaches the 6.38 target; and explains a specific strength-versus-cost tradeoff. Partial credit: Correct method or useful comparisons but missing a design, calculation, target, or tradeoff explanation. No credit: Gives no usable calculations or selects a winner solely by clip count without considering cost.
